text: Scene 10 - Basil’s revelation
speaker: C5

text: Next morning his butler announced the arrival of Basil Hallward.
speaker: C6

text: Basil’s face was grave. He advanced taking both of Dorian's hands in his.
speaker: C8

text: I am so glad I have found you. I called last night after reading of the terrible tragedy. They told me you were at the opera. Of course I knew that was impossible and surmised you must be with that poor girl's mother. What a state she must be in - and her only child too. What did she say?
speaker: Basil

text: My dear fellow, how do I know? I was at the opera. You should have come too. I met Lady Gwendolen, Harry's sister. She is perfectly charming and Patti sang divinely. Please don't talk of horrid subjects - if one doesn't think about it, it has never happened. I may mention that she was not the woman's only child - she has a son who is a James.
speaker: Dorian

text: You went to the opera while Sybil Vane was lying in some sordid lodging. You talk of other women being charming before the girl you loved has even the quiet of a grave to sleep in?
speaker: Basil

text: Stop Basil! What's done is done. What's past is past.
speaker: Dorian

text: You call yesterday the past?
speaker: Basil

text: What has the actual lapse of time got to do with it? It is only shallow people who require years to get rid of an emotion. I don't want to be at the mercy of my emotions, I want to use them, enjoy them and dominate them.
speaker: Dorian

text: I don't know what has come over you. You look exactly like the same wonderful boy who came to my studio. You were the most unspoiled creature in the whole world. It is all Harry's influence I see that.
speaker: Basil

text: I owe Harry a great deal and I don't know what you want of me.
speaker: Dorian

text: I want the Dorian I used to paint. I'm afraid this tragedy has unhinged your beautiful mind. You talk as if you have no heart - no pity in you.
speaker: Basil

text: You must not think I have not suffered. If you had come yesterday perhaps at half past five or a quarter to six you would have found me in tears. Even Harry had no idea what I was going through. I suffered immensely and then it passed. I cannot repeat an emotion no-one can except sentimentalists.
speaker: Dorian

text: What has happened to you my dear boy?
speaker: Basil

text: I was a boy when you first knew me. I am a man now. I have new passions, new thoughts, new ideas. I am changed but you must always be my friend. I am fond of Harry but you are better than him. Not stronger - you are too much afraid of life, but you are better. Don't leave me Basil - I am what I am.
speaker: Dorian

text: The painter was strangely moved.
speaker: C5

text: The lad was infinitely dear to him He could not bear to reproach him anymore.
speaker: C6

text: He knew there was so much in him that was good and noble.
speaker: C8

text: I'll speak no more of this horrible thing. I only trust your name will not be mentioned. The inquest is to take place this afternoon. Have they summoned you?
speaker: Basil

text: They don't know my name. Sybil only referred to me as her Prince Charming. It was so pretty of her - you must do me a drawing of Sybil - I would like something more than the memory of a few kisses and broken pathetic words.
speaker: Dorian

text: I will try and do something if that would please you but you must come and sit for me again. I can't get on without you.
speaker: Basil

text: I can never sit for you again. It's impossible.
speaker: Dorian

text: Don't you like what I did of you? Is that why you have it covered?
speaker: Basil

text: You must not look at it. I don't wish you to. If you try to look at it I will never speak to you again.
speaker: Dorian

text: Of course I won't if that's what you want but Georges Petit is to exhibit all my best pictures in Paris - it would only be away for a month. This is my best work and...
speaker: Basil

text: You told me a month ago that you would never exhibit it. Why have you changed your mind? You told Harry the same thing - that nothing would induce you to...
speaker: Dorian

text: He stopped suddenly - a gleam of light came into his eyes.
speaker: C5

text: He remembered what Lord Henry had told him half seriously and half in jest.
speaker: C6

text: If you want a strange quarter of an hour, get Basil to tell you why he won't exhibit your picture. He told me and it was something of a revelation.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: Perhaps Basil had his secrets too.
speaker: C8

text: We each of us seem to have a secret - tell me yours and I will tell you mine. Why did you not exhibit my picture?
speaker: Dorian

text: If I told you you might like me less than you do or laugh at me and I could not bear it. If you wish me to never look at your picture again I am content. I will always have you to look at. your friendship is dearer to me than any fame.
speaker: Basil

text: I think I have the right to know why you would not exhibit it.
speaker: Dorian

text: Answer me one thing. Have you ever noticed something curious in the picture? I see you have - no don't speak, wait till you hear what I have to say. From the moment I met you you have had the most extraordinary influence over me. I was dominated, soul, brain and power by you. I worshipped you. I grew jealous of every one to whom you spoke. I wanted to have you all to myself and was only happy when I was with you. The world had become wonderful to my eyes - too wonderful perhaps for in such mad worships there is peril.
speaker: Basil

text: I don't/
speaker: Dorian

text: / let me finish while I have the courage. As I worked on your portrait, every flake and film of colour seemed to reveal my secret.I became afraid that the world would see my idolatry. I felt that I had told too much. I find it extraordinary that you should also have seen this in the portrait.
speaker: Basil

text: I saw something in it - something that made me curious.
speaker: Dorian

text: Well you won't mind my looking at it now?
speaker: Basil

text: You must not ask me. I cannot ever let you stand in front of that picture again.
speaker: Dorian

text: Perhaps you are right. You have been the one person in my life to influence my art. You don't know how much it has cost me to reveal myself to you.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian drew a long breath.
speaker: C4

text: The colour came back to his cheeks.
speaker: C5

text: A smile played on his lips.
speaker: C6

text: The peril was over. He was safe for the time.
speaker: All

text: What have you told me? Simply that you felt you admired me too much. But you mustn't talk of worship. It is foolish. You and I are friends Basil and we must always remain so.
speaker: Dorian

text: You have got Harry.
speaker: Basil

text: Oh Harry! He spends his days saying what is incredible and his evenings doing what is improbable.
speaker: Dorian

text: You will sit for me again?
speaker: Basil

text: I must never sit for you again. There is something fatal about a portrait. It has a life of its own.
speaker: Dorian

text: I'm sorry you won't let me look at the picture once again but I understand what you feel about it. I’m sorry - I must go.
speaker: Basil

text: As he left the room Dorian smiled to himself. Instead of being forced to reveal his own secret he had wrested a secret from his friend.
speaker: C5

text: But the portrait must now be hidden away at all costs.
speaker: C8

text: He could not run the risk of discovery again.
speaker: C5

text: He rang the bell for his housekeeper.
speaker: C6

text: After a few moments, Mrs. Leaf bustled into the library.
speaker: Mrs Leaf

text: He asked her for the key of the schoolroom.
speaker: C6

text: The old schoolroom, Mr Dorian? Why, it is full of dust. I must put it straight before you go into it. It is not fit for you to see, sir.
speaker: Mrs Leaf

text: I don't want it put straight, Leaf. I only want the key.
speaker: Dorian

text: Well, sir, you'll be covered with cobwebs if you go into it. Why, it hasn't been opened for nearly five years - not since his lordship died.
speaker: Mrs Leaf

text: That does not matter. Give me the key.
speaker: Dorian

text: And here is the key, sir I’ll have it off the bunch in a moment. But you don't think of living up there, sir, and you so comfortable here?
speaker: Mrs Leaf

text: No, no. Thank you, Leaf. That will do. Send Peter and John to me.
speaker: Dorian

text: Very good sir.
speaker: Mrs Leaf

text: Oh Sir - I quite forgot. Lord Wotton left something for you.
speaker: Mrs Leaf
